# Animation Systems

> **Draft chapter map.** Explain animation as data transformation from authored clips and graph state to pose data and renderable deformation.

## Animation Has Several Consumers

- Distinguish gameplay meaning, pose evaluation, physics interaction, and visual deformation.
- Explain why a single skeletal object should not be mutated freely by every subsystem.

### Poses, Clips, and Blending

- Introduce local poses, global transforms, clip sampling, and blend operations.
- Connect the data model to predictable performance and authoring.

#### State Machines and Animation Graphs

- Explain declarative transition logic and parameter-driven graph evaluation.
- Compare authored graph data with hard-coded behavior.

## Moving Information Across Boundaries

- Explain root motion, events, sockets, and attachment points as explicit contracts.
- Identify which facts affect gameplay and which are render-only.

### Deformation and the Render Domain

- Trace the path from a computed pose to skinned or deformed geometry.
- Connect palette data to the render-thread firewall.

#### Inverse Kinematics and Procedural Adjustment

- Present IK as an additional pose transformation with clear ownership.
- Discuss quality, latency, and debugging trade-offs.

## Scaling Animated Worlds

- Cover update-rate policy, LOD, pose sharing, and crowd behavior.
- Connect animation cost to visibility and streaming demand.

### Smallworld’s Animation Direction

- Use the engine as a concrete implementation example when the abstractions are established.
- Identify open design choices separately from durable architecture.

#### Diagnostics and Authoring Feedback

- Outline pose visualizers, graph traces, and event inspection.
- Relate tool support to reliable content iteration.
